- Contract language: we should avoid absolutes like "never" for telemetry; instead use measurable SLAs and bounded exceptions. - Define "telemetry" precisely: metrics/traces/exposed application-level logs for observability vs. customer content (inputs/outputs). The annex must explicitly state that customer content is never routed outside APAC except as required by law/with consent.
- Evidence: attach a simple controls matrix listing encryption-at-rest, KMS key locality, and access controls for any centralized analytics tenant.

I will draft the annex language and the controls matrix. Soojin, please confirm that the infra can support a max 4-hour buffer and what operational signals would trigger an automatic extension (e.g., active node failover vs. extended region outage).

Quick ops note —

We can implement the proposed transient-buffering model. Details:
- Normal path: telemetry ingestion endpoints in APAC regions (Tokyo/Singapore) owned by the customer tenancy for Aurelia. Aggregation and analytics run on regional clusters.
- Failover path: if entire APAC AZ/region experiences outage, telemetry ingestion will be re-routed to our centralized analytics tenancy in us-central for the purpose of diagnostics and cluster recovery.
- Maximum TTL: we can limit non-APAC retention to 4 hours by default. After 4 hours, data is automatically purged unless Aurelia approves a manual extension via the incident channel.
- Access controls: centralized tenancy uses separate KMS keys scoped to emergency diagnostics; access is restricted to named SREs and audited.

I will prepare the operational diagram and a terse playbook explaining the notification cadence and purge process.
